first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value, adoption, and SMB activation. It is more aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. Verify onboarding and activation-messaging records because they are the two strongest sustainable responses to the linked onboarding and activation declines; current preference is onboarding simplification, subject to those source details.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and previously delivered completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, making it the strongest option for sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Activation messaging is credible but produced a smaller retention lift. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its known retention harm conflicts with the primary objective.

final2.rationale: Switch to a tightly targeted promotional-pricing test for price-sensitive SMB accounts showing credible churn intent. The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled churn conversations create an immediate revenue-retention threat, while prior evidence shows this segment responds strongly to pricing. Because that evidence also showed materially worse 30-day retention, do not roll out broadly: constrain eligibility, duration, and discount depth, and judge success on retained qualified revenue and downstream retention—not short-term conversion alone.
